limitations: The fixed exact numerical acceptance contract failed; normal device exit and intact guards do not turn it into an accepted performance result.
The CPU FP32 replay and exact dyadic bounds describe a reference calculation, not the undocumented internal WMMA arithmetic.
No attribution to hardware, compiler or library defect is established by the observed residuals.
A float accumulator type alone does not establish strict IEEE FP32 intermediate rounding or an error bound for this matrix primitive.
Reproduction comparisons report direct equality of actual retained words and mismatch coordinates; agreement or disagreement is not forced.
Only final repeated-launch outputs are retained; no arbitrary FP16 input, nonzero initial accumulator, other target or target-framework qualification.
Pointer alignments, resources and recompile flags are observations, not hardware requirements, physical allocation, actual residency or compilation counts.
CPU packing and transfers are excluded from recorded event intervals; timing is not accepted as performance evidence.
